final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: 3.6% dairy TRQ, 73/74/75% auto RVC phase-in with year-two audit start, automatic labor penalties in binding text, Chapter 19 retained for investment/IP, five-year sunset review with renewal presumption, and self-certification with spot-checks in year one. Simultaneous trilateral signing agreed for next round.
minority_objections: USTR initially pushed bilateral-first sequencing (Mexico signs, Canada joins later), rejected by Congress and Canada
Dairy demanded higher market access numbers beyond 3.6% TRQ but was overruled by package momentum
key_conflicts: Canada's Chapter 19 red line vs. USTR's initial rejection of binational panels
Dairy supply management market access vs. Canada's political sensitivity
Hard sunset clause vs. business demand for investment certainty
Year-one audit timing vs. auto industry's supply chain retooling needs
Bilateral-first sequencing vs. Canada's demand for simultaneous trilateral signing
key_concessions: USTR accepted Chapter 19 retention for investment/IP disputes (moved from 'off the table' to hybrid model)
USTR moved from hard five-year sunset to review-with-renewal-presumption
Auto industry accepted 75% final RVC target in exchange for three-year phase-in and year-two audit start
All parties accepted automatic penalties for labor violations (no post-finding negotiation)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 binational panels must remain for non-labor disputes
Canada: dairy supply management cannot face unlimited market access
USTR: labor enforcement must be binding treaty text with automatic penalties
Congress: no ratification without binding enforcement language locked before signing
Labor unions: enforcement mechanism must be in treaty text, not side letters
Auto industry: cannot hit 75% RVC without phase-in period
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Compliance checkpoint mechanism (self-cert with spot-checks) only surfaced in final round after auto/labor raised year-three penalty cliff risk
Specific fluid milk and cheese import numbers within 3.6% TRQ left vague
Enforcement body composition and penalty schedule details deferred to binding text drafting
Mexico's domestic ratification risk mentioned once but never explored as constraint
downstream_risk_variables: Whether 3.6% dairy TRQ is politically sellable in Canada beyond this negotiating room
Whether self-certification regime creates loopholes or compliance gaming
Whether five-year review triggers actual renegotiation pressure despite renewal presumption
Whether automatic penalty schedule is calibrated to avoid triggering withdrawal
Whether Mexico's Congress ratifies identical terms to U.S.-Canada package
uncertainty_notes: Binding text drafting deferred to next round; enforcement body penalty schedule and composition unspecified; dairy TRQ subcategory allocations (fluid milk vs. cheese) not detailed; self-certification audit sampling rate and triggers undefined; renewal presumption's legal enforceability unclear.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC drove the three-year phase-in compromise (73/74/75), year-two audit deferral, and self-cert mechanism—auto industry's compliance concerns directly shaped final package structure
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Binding treaty text with automatic penalties became Congress and labor's explicit ratification threshold—USTR moved from vague 'inspections' to locked enforcement language to secure votes
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: 3.6% TRQ discussed and accepted by Canada, but dairy ag pushed for higher numbers and was overruled—raised as concern but did not block the deal
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'off the table' as non-negotiable; USTR's initial rejection triggered hybrid compromise (Chapter 19 for investment/IP, new body for labor)—drove concrete proposal change
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard five-year renegotiation clause explicitly rejected by manufacturers as investment-killing; USTR moved to review-with-renewal-presumption to secure business support—drove sunset clause redesign
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated 'won't ratify on handshake' and demanded binding text before signing; labor and Congress both made ratification contingent on locked enforcement language—shaped sequencing and text-locking timeline
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto and supply-chain manufacturers raised retooling costs and sourcing timelines, secured phase-in and audit deferral—acknowledged and accommodated but did not drive overall deal structure
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico proposed bilateral signing first with Canada joining later; Congress and Canada rejected sequencing as politically unratifiable—raised but abandoned, did not shape final outcome

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
